subject: Unified offer surface + cloud-specific tweaks for marketplace listings
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unified offer surface + cloud-specific tweaks for marketplace listings

Team —

Quick summary: as we expand listings across AWS, Azure, and GCP we are seeing an explosion of variants. Left unchecked that will fragment co-sell signals and make enablement harder. I put together a lean proposal (attached) to create a single canonical offer surface with 3 primary SKUs and lightweight cloud-specific tweaks (labeling, region defaults, bundling rules).

Goals for this thread:
- Agree the canonical SKUs we will publish (hosted SaaS, Dedicated Reserved, Private/VPC on-prem).
- Decide which cloud-specific variants we tolerate (e.g., AZURE: marketplace-native SaaS vs. bring-your-own-infra).
- Set regional launch priorities for canaries (which regions per cloud to go live first).
- Define co-sell triggers (ACV, committed usage, pilot success criteria) and a fallback policy if a cloud SKU is unavailable.

Attachments: redwood_sku_matrix_v3.xlsx (versioned by SKU, proposed SKU-to-cloud mapping), marketplace_listing_checklist.docx

Ask: please review and reply with concrete preferences by end of day Tuesday 9/21. If you think a short sync is needed, suggest times — I'm tentatively blocking 60m on Wednesday.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Marketplace GTM | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unified offer surface + cloud-specific tweaks for marketplace listings

+1 to the canonical SKUs. A few practical suggestions after skimming the matrix:

- Canonical SKU names (keep short): Redwood-Hosted, Redwood-Dedicated, Redwood-Private. Add an "Optimize" add-on SKU for quantization/optimizations (useful for cost-led co-sell decks).
- Cloud-specific variants: allow label-only variants (e.g., "Redwood-Hosted (Azure SaaS)") rather than full SKU proliferation. That keeps reporting clean but satisfies listing UX.
- Regions: propose US (us-east-1), EU (westeurope / eu-west-1), APAC (asia-southeast1) as the initial three canary buckets — but stagger by cloud: AWS: us-east-1 + eu-west-1 first; Azure: westeurope + eastus2; GCP: us-central1 + europe-west3.
- Co-sell triggers: recommend ACV >= $250k or committed GPU months >= 12 OR a validated integration with partner sales lead. For lower ACV, require Marketplace listing + joint case study before co-sell.
- Fallback policy: if a cloud-specific listing fails verification or capacity issues, route leads to Redwood-Hosted (global) and mark for sales handoff.

I've updated the attached sheet with a proposed SKU naming convention and sample HubSpot fields. See my comments in red.

Jonas

Head of Partner GTM | Redwood Inference

Subject: Marketplace packaging: ask for constraints and co-sell criteria (Redwood proposals attached)

Hi Sanjay / Elena / Marco —

Thanks again for the early product calls last week. We're formalizing a concise decision set for our marketplace listings and co-sell gating and would appreciate confirmation on a few constraints from each cloud team. Short list below; attached is our SKU matrix (redwood_sku_matrix_v3.xlsx).

Key questions:
1) Marketplace packaging constraints: are there limits on number of SKUs, or naming conventions we must follow per cloud? Any disallowed metadata fields?
2) Listing form requirements: for SaaS vs. AMI/container listings do you require separate artifacts (example: AWS requires AMI/CloudFormation + SaaS listing)?
3) Co-sell enablement: what is your minimum qualification for listing-driven co-sell? ACV, technical validation, reference customer? What enablement packets do you expect from us?
4) Regional recommendations: any capacity or compliance blockers you recommend we avoid for initial canaries?

We're aiming to launch first canaries within 6 weeks after sign-off and would prefer a small, consistent SKU surface across clouds. Short reply with bullets is perfect. If useful, happy to schedule a 30-min alignment call.

Cheers,
Hannah

From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@amazon.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 10:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging: ask for constraints and co-sell criteria (Redwood proposals attached)

Hannah —

Appreciate the crisp ask. Quick bullets from the AWS Marketplace team: 

- SKU counts: no hard upper limit but simpler is better. We recommend 3–5 SKUs per product for discoverability. Avoid per-region SKU splits; instead use listing attributes/regions list.
- Packaging: for SaaS listings we need a SaaS product entry (with subscription metadata) + a manifest (billing endpoint). For AMI/container marketplace items you submit AMIs/containers. If your Hosted product is true SaaS, one SaaS listing suffices.
- Naming: keep SKU labels concise, but include an attribute for "Deployment Type" in metadata (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Co-sell: qualification is typically ACV >= $200k or track record with a validated architecture + one customer reference. AWS can fast-track if you provide a solution brief, technical architecture diagram, and a reference customer. We'll also need the AWS co-sell intake form (I attached a template).
- Regions: for canaries we suggest us-east-1 + eu-west-1. Avoid specialized regions with custom compliance unless you have a mapped data residency plan.

I'll share this with our co-sell enablement folks — if you can provide the solution brief and the listing draft, we can slot a joint enablement session.

Best,
Sanjay Mehta
Partner Solutions Manager, AWS ISV
sanjay.mehta@amazon.com
Amazon Web Services

Attachment: aws-co-sell-template.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unified offer surface + cloud-specific tweaks for marketplace listings — decisions + next actions

Team — thanks for the feedback and Sanjay's quick reply. Proposed decisions to lock in (we'll publish an internal decision doc after this):

1) SKUs: adopt the canonical three + Optimize add-on as Jonas suggested: Redwood-Hosted, Redwood-Dedicated, Redwood-Private, Redwood-Optimize (add-on).
2) Cloud variants: allow label-only variants where required by cloud UX (e.g., "Redwood-Hosted (Azure SaaS)") but maintain 1 reporting SKU in HubSpot.
3) Regions & canary plan:
   - AWS: launch canary in us-east-1 + eu-west-1.
   - Azure: launch canary in eastus2 + westeurope.
   - GCP: launch canary in us-central1 + europe-west3.
   Staggered rollout over 6 weeks; first go-live target: 2027-11-01 for AWS canary.
4) Co-sell triggers: ACV >= $225k OR 12+ committed GPU months OR validated reference + solution brief. Lower ACV opportunities get marketplace listing + joint case study before co-sell.
5) Fallback routing: route to Redwood-Hosted global listing and create an internal sprint to resolve the cloud-specific blocker.

Next actions (owners):
- Karthik: prepare listing drafts (all clouds) and the solution brief draft. Attach to HubSpot deal RED-54211.
- Jonas: update SKU matrix and finalize HubSpot property mapping.
- Hannah: schedule a 45-min partner alignment on 9/23 at 11:00 PT (tentative).
- Ben: own canary runbook and validate telemetry hooks (cost & latency) for listing-level pages.

I'll publish the decision doc and updated attachments after you ack.

Ben Carter
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
